SMTO-SKL-0048 — Google Drive asked SMTO to slow down

GUID: bc3079cb-fb17-558b-8418-e1009678c0d7
Slug: google-drive-rate-limited
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-drive

What happened

  • Google limits how many Drive requests an account or app can make in a short time, and that limit was reached. SMTO already retried reads briefly; it never repeats changes on its own.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait a few minutes and avoid running other big Drive tasks with the same account during that time. Google lifts the limit after a short pause once requests slow down.
  2. If you asked SMTO to change, upload or move something, open Google Drive and check whether that change is already there. Repeating a change that already happened can create duplicates or undo other edits.
  3. Then ask SMTO again, for fewer files at a time if the request covered many. Smaller requests are less likely to hit the limit again.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the request without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; Google's usage limits for SMTO's Google app may need to be raised. Don't keep resending the request quickly.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google Drive returned HTTP 429 or a rate/quota reason (rateLimitExceeded, userRateLimitExceeded, quotaExceeded) after SMTO's bounded read retries, or on a write that is never retried automatically.

What this means

  • Google returns HTTP 429 or a recognized rate/quota-limit reason. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Google returns HTTP 429 or a recognized rate/quota-limit reason.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect Retry-After and safe provider reason; write uncertainty is a separate outcome.

How to fix it

  • provider_error mapped 429/quota reasons to rate_limited. Reads are retried up to twice, and only when Retry-After is absent or at most 5 s; writes are never retried. Wait for the provider's retry interval, check the Google Cloud quota for the OAuth app if it recurs, and for writes confirm the change did not already apply before repeating.
  • Wait for the provider retry interval. Reads have bounded retries; inspect uncertain writes before retrying.

Retry and execution caution

  • Wait for the provider retry interval. Reads have bounded retries; inspect uncertain writes before retrying.

How to verify the fix

  • A later permitted request respects the interval and existing mutation receipts.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials, content or resumable URLs.
  • Do not blindly repeat uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
